newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices mixed, Gulf loses ground.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices mixed, Gulf loses ground.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mixed Tuesday, with mild East Coast weather pressuring values at the Gulf, while cooler Midwest temperatures helped firm prices slightly there, industry sources said.
Traders also said slower injections in the East were forcing more gas on the market, while some light Midwest heating loads could pick up some of the slack in that region.
"There are people (in the Midwest) turning their heaters on," said one cash trader, noting cool forecasts this week.
U.S. Gulf Coast prices slipped two cents today to the mid-to-high-$1.80s/mmBtu, still eight cents over Sept indices.
October gas at the Gulf was now pegged at even to NYMEX to 10 cents under the screen, or on either side of $1.80 and still slightly over Sept 1 levels.
But without some cold weather next month, most agreed tapering injections could pressure the physical market.
Midcontinent gas was steady to up slightly in the mid-$1.70s, almost 10 cents over Sept 1, while October flows on the same pipes were quoted at 17-19 cents under the screen.

In west Texas, El Paso Permian was unchanged to modestly higher in the high-$1.60s, more than five cents over index. South Texas gas also was up slightly in the low-$1.80s, more than five cents over first of the month prices. October gas in south Texas was quoted at 11 to 12 cents under NYMEX.
October New York city gate gas was pegged at about 20 cents over the screen, or about the $2.05 area.
